buildMethod: Pinned optimized/static no-symbol flags; one compiler. Core, Duplicates and Bridge plus twenty-two targets compile fresh. Thirty-nine unchanged shared core hashes retained. Shared media helpers; no installer package.
proof: Paired replacement releases the publisher model mutex for intent existence/serialization/durable write, final source/directory/original checks, ReplaceFile, final catalog serialization/write and journal cleanup. Runtime ownership covers both records, current target and previous-version path throughout. Original size comes from its protected preflight handle rather than a filesystem query inside the final model section.

One CommitId/PublicationCommitId binds the new row and relocated original row. A single proof entry requires both exact projections in one actual successful catalog snapshot. Missing or changed companion rows reject before capture; a primary-only, companion-only or unrelated newer sequence cannot prove completion. Group ownership also excludes a competing proof on the companion record.

Completion-owned deltas apply to fresh current rows. A containing newer write can prove success after the original fails or is superseded. An unacknowledged outcome conditionally restores matching new-row completion contributions while keeping the original bound to its actual previous-version file. Independent metadata/settings remain current. It retains both complete versions and the journal instead of reversing a potentially acknowledged swap. Explicit recovery through either visible record or restart resolves the pair.

New-format replacement recovery validates both identities, bound destinations and hashes, rejects newer completion stamps, preserves already accepted current queue/scanner metadata for both records, and otherwise merges the operation into current metadata. Partial exact rows retain later accepted queue/scanner choices. Scoped recovery matches either the new Id or OriginalId. Original relocation applies only its owned file/history fields, preserving unrelated current metadata. Legacy journals retain their existing recovery branch. Internal unregistered replacement output pairs a private receipt with the exact visible original; it adds no phantom download row. Receipt cleanup now also respects pending replacement journals.

296 paired checks exercise actual detached intent/move/snapshot/flush/post-write-pre-ack/cleanup gates; both-record model access and guards; metadata and settings; failed/lost/deferred save outcomes; newer containing success and supersession; private internal success/failure/lost-ack/unlink; denied journal removal; malformed/newer identity rejection; later queue and scanner choices; reopening; original-scoped dependent recovery, correct original target before recovery, original metadata during intent I/O, and four owned crash subprocess boundaries.

All 1,599 focused checks pass, including the existing 347 ordinary/child publication and 186 ownership checks, 46 coordinator/proof checks and 261 completion checks through observed exit 0. Twenty-two binaries have verified 8.16 resources/hashes, 482 inputs and 42 reusable core objects. Core, Duplicates and Bridge rebuild; 39 unchanged core hashes are retained. Shared media tools have zero new copies.

limits: Recovery filesystem/hash/save work and initial protected-directory handle checks still retain their existing model locks. Outer recursive-lock callers cannot gain responsiveness from releasing only the publisher inner acquisition. Generic raw model/graph mutation and all ingress/lifecycle paths are not exhaustively qualified.

An uncertain paired catalog failure keeps both versions at their final target/previous paths and retains the journal; the incomplete new row requires recovery while live original history remains bound to its old bytes. This deliberately replaces the old best-effort physical reverse-swap behavior, which could reverse a swap whose containing catalog write was already successful but unacknowledged.

Four registered-pair process crash boundaries are tested, not physical power loss. Recovery through an original record cannot update an unregistered external JobPtr no longer owned by Manager; it reconciles visible history and files without a phantom row. Private-pair process crashes, broad media/live/prefetch/stop/volume matrices and external reparse/source-delete-sharing/namespace races remain unqualified. Existing ReplaceFile flags and source/directory protections are preserved; no new hardware durability or zero-delay guarantee.

Chained transactions with an earlier surviving ordinary/replacement journal on the original need dedicated lineage/reconciliation checks; current gates qualify one paired intent and its recovery, not arbitrary journal chains.
